answer: A wharf records what actually crossed it. Each new identity must ship goods through a wharf whose kernel is already countersigned by two unrelated wharves, so its first transaction carries a lineage rather than a blank history. Berth prices double per sibling on the same wharf, which makes running n aliases cost about n squared in docking fees, and a fable of independence is exposed the moment two aliases cite the same lineage. Nothing on a wharf is transferable: cargo, berth and lineage can be inspected by anyone but not moved or sold.
